notes: Primary ask: dedicated capacity planning + SLOs for enterprise customers (they consult for 10+ fintech clients).
Workload profile (from client telemetry): median request size ~ 220 tokens; p95 ~ 820 tokens; avg tokens/request ~ 300
Baseline steady-state: 12 QPS across pooled tenants (expected to grow). Peak bursts seen up to 180 QPS (30s spikes) during market open windows.
Target latency SLOs: 95th < 250ms for short-chat responses (<128 tokens), p95 < 800ms for median multi-turn (300 tokens). Cost sensitivity: medium-to-high — customers care about $/1000 tokens.
Model preference: open-model family; prefer 70B-class quantized runtimes for cost balance. Want ability to fallback to smaller q4 variants on capacity pressure.
Routing/fallback: region-aware routing (NA primary, EU for regional clients), automatic fallback to warm quantized model variants, preferrer caching for common prefixes.
SLA negotiation points flagged: uptime target 99.95% (vs Redwood default 99.9); credits for latency SLO misses, on-call escalation window, maintenance blackout windows for market hours.

Reserved GPU planning notes: initial rough estimate = 6 x A100-80GB equiv to cover steady + 25% headroom for median workloads at target QPS; peak planning requires burst pool (2-3 GPUs) or autoscale burst to cheaper capacity.

Sizing assumption callouts: KV cache hit expected ~35% on re-runs; batching expected to reduce per-token cost by 18% at steady state; token/sec per GPU estimated from model perf runs (internal numbers attached).
Security notes: require customer-managed KMS for on-prem projects; need SOC2 attestation copy before procurement signs; data residency requests for two EU clients (Paris, Frankfurt).
Customer quote (paraphrase): 'We need predictable per-customer latency guarantees so our SLAs to end-customers hold during market spikes.'
POC ask: 2-week dedicated trial with telemetry export and per-token cost breakdown; include trace samples for p95 analysis.
workshop_highlights: Focused on baseline QPS vs peak: validated steady 12 QPS and short spikes to 180 QPS using replayed traces.
Token/sec profiling: avg 300 tokens/request -> ~3600 tokens/sec at steady 12 QPS; peak token/sec observed ~54k during bursts.
Kernel/quantization notes: 4-bit quantized variants reduce memory footprint and enable more concurrent streams but increase latency variance slightly.
Batching strategy: recommend mixed batching policy — 50ms max latency wait, adaptive batching under high load; expect 15-20% cost savings without breaking p95 SLO.
KV caching: prefix cache for 20% of requests gave 30% latency improvement for repeated sessions in test.
Suggested reserve: two pools — steady (reserved) sized for 12-25 QPS sustained, burst pool for 180+ spikes handled by autoscale or contractual burst capacity.
SLA template items: per-route latency SLOs, regional capacity commitments, incident MTTR < 2 hours for severity-1, annual maintenance windows defined, financial credits tied to p95 misses.
Deliverables agreed: sizing spreadsheet, runbook for failover to quantized variants, draft SLA redlines, POC agreement for 14-day trial.
